You are the track lead of track D (docs) in a multi-session refactoring round of treams-rs (github.com/yaugenst/treams-rs). This work is coordinated by a lead session, which spawned you. It cannot receive messages from you. You communicate through git: your work branch, your tooling branch and status files.

What the round is about

The owner is open-sourcing treams-rs. The codebase must be clean, consistently named and well documented. The documentation is your part. In the owner's words: "documentation should also be well organized. we do not have to make pretty docs but basic docs with examples as well as rationale on github pages would very helpful. basically the complete thing anyone would need who is familiar with treams, and needs to learn about treams-rs."

The site is MkDocs Material on GitHub Pages:

  • Deployment is gated by the repository variable DOCS_DEPLOY, so nothing publishes until the owner enables it.
  • Repository: https://github.com/yaugenst/treams-rs. Site: https://yaugenst.github.io/treams-rs.

No numerical change is allowed anywhere. A detailed, binding plan with 93 work packages already exists.

Setup (do this first)

cd treams-rs
git fetch origin r4-tooling
git show origin/r4-tooling:setup.sh > scratch: r4-setup.sh
bash scratch: r4-setup.sh docs

If the repository is not at treams-rs, set REPO=<path> for setup.sh. setup.sh is idempotent. If a step fails because of the environment, fix the environment, rerun it, and note what you changed. Do not change the gates. setup.sh also clones upstream treams at the pinned commit to scratch: treams. Its docs/examples and notebooks are the source of the example gallery.

Then read, in this order:

  1. README.md: the session protocol, working loop, integration gate and rules.
  2. plan/decisions.md: owner decisions, defaults, out-of-scope items and hard gates.
  3. plan/tracks.md: your packages, their order and cross-track dependencies.
  4. plan/plan.md: §2, §4 (glossary), §5, §6.3 (docs site tree), §7, §8 and §9.

The work-package briefs are plan/wp/<ID>.json. After setup, all of these are also reachable at wps/round4/.

Your packages (plan/tracks.md, track D)

  • First: P08 → D03 → D04, then D06 → D07 and R01.
    • D04 is on the Python track's critical path (D05 and P16 wait for it). Push it and record it ready as soon as it is approved and gated.
    • P08 and D03 need P07, which the lead is merging (stage 2) right now.
  • Later, as their cross-track dependencies arrive: D10, D11, D12, D13, D14, D15, D17, D08, D09, D16.
    • They depend on final Python names (P17, P24, D05 from the Python session) and final native and Rust names (P19, R16, R28, R32a, R33, R36, R40, R51, R52, R54 from the lead).
    • Order them by what has arrived.
  • D18 (final sweep) runs last, after every other package of every track is merged.

Do not start any package before r4sync.sh merged lists all of its cross-track dependencies and you have run r4sync.sh pull. While you wait, use the send_later tool (claude-code-remote MCP server) to schedule a check-in about every 60 minutes. Never idle-poll with sleep.

How to work

Follow the working loop in README.md:

  • sync with r4sync.sh pull;
  • create lanes as worktrees under scratch: lanes/;
  • run the Workflow tool with scriptPath scratch: implement_round4.js and args {lanes: [{name, worktree, branch, wps: [{id, title, profile}]}]} (title and gate_profile come from each wp file); it implements, adversarially reviews and fixes each package;
  • inspect the verdicts;
  • merge the lanes into your work branch claude/r4-docs;
  • run the full integration gate in the main checkout (including mkdocs build --strict once mkdocs.yml exists);
  • push the work branch;
  • record the packages with r4sync.sh ready <IDs>.

Use at most 3 concurrent lanes (4 CPUs). Remove lane worktrees after merging.

Rules

  • Push only to claude/r4-docs (work) and r4-tooling-docs (tooling and status). You have explicit permission for both.
  • Never push to claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh or r4-tooling, which belong to the lead.
  • Never open pull requests, never force-push, never rewrite history.
  • Commits are signed automatically. Use your session's attribution trailers, and never put model names in commits or code.
  • Never modify benchmarks/results/**.
  • Never enable or trigger a Pages deployment.
  • Packages that are not approved are not marked ready.
  • When the track is complete, write status/docs-report.md in your tooling branch and push it. Cover each package's outcome, open issues for the lead, deviations from the plan and what was not verified.
  • Work autonomously. Nobody will answer questions. Where the plan leaves a choice open, decide in its spirit and record the decision in your report.
